questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. When the District Attorney asked the convict about details of the day of the crime, he started beating about the bush .
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence.

When the District Attorney asked the convict about details of the day of the crime, he started beating about the bush.

options.text: Speaking in a confusing manner without giving a correct answer
options.html: Speaking in a confusing manner without giving a correct answer

questions.solution:
The idiom 'beating about the bush' means 'to avoid talking about what is important'.

Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Old wives' tale
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Old wives' tale

options.text: a common belief little confirmed by science
options.html: a common belief little confirmed by science

questions.solution: The idiom 'old wives' tale' refers to a superstitious belief that is not confirmed by science. E.g. The idea that drinking alcohol will cure the flu is an old wives' tale, nothing more. D is the right answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Like a bull in a China shop
questions.questionHtml:

Like a bull in a China shop

options.text: Cannot be trusted or relied upon
options.html: Cannot be trusted or relied upon

questions.solution:
Like a bull in a China shop: Behaving clumsily or recklessly in a delicate or sensitive situation.

Among the given options, 'act awkwardly and carelessly' is the correct meaning of the given idiom.

Hence, the correct answer is option (d).

questions.question: Choose the correct meaning of the phrase. Once bitten, twice shy.
questions.questionHtml:
Choose the correct meaning of the phrase.

Once bitten, twice shy.

options.text: A bad experience makes you wary of the same thing happening again.
options.html: A bad experience makes you wary of the same thing happening again.

options.text: Bitten by an animal that makes you sick.
options.html: Bitten by an animal that makes you sick.

questions.solution:
The phrase 'once bitten, twice shy' means a bad experience that makes you wary of the same thing happening again.

Usage - He was two days late last time, so she's not hiring him again - once bitten, twice shy.

Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute italicised words in the given sentence The one-hour period after his lunch is his time for a short sleep .
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute italicised words in the given sentence

The one-hour period after his lunch is his time for a short sleep.
questions.solution:
Option (d) is the correct answer.

The idiom 'forty winks' means 'a short sleep, especially during the day'.

The meanings of the other idioms are-

On thin ice means- in a risky situation.

Once in a blue moon means - rarely.

On cloud nine- extremely happy.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the boldened/underlined idiom. He has no political axe to grind , he is just concerned about the state of affairs here.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the boldened/underlined idiom.

He has no political axe to grind, he is just concerned about the state of affairs here.

options.text: To do hard work at the last moment
options.html: To do hard work at the last moment

questions.solution:
The idiom 'an axe to grind' means a selfish aim or motive. So, 'a private interest to serve' is the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Hence, option (a) is the correct choice.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Bide one's time.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Bide one's time.

options.text: Wasting all the time and worrying later.
options.html: Wasting all the time and worrying later.

questions.solution:
The meaning of the idiom 'bide one's time' is 'wait quietly for a good opportunity to do something'. Accordingly, the correct answer is given in option (c), 'waiting for the right opportunity'.

Hence, the correct answer is option (c).

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. In the doldrums
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

In the doldrums

options.text: Doing something poorly in order to save time or money
options.html: Doing something poorly in order to save time or money

options.text: To appear in a way or make an impression that causes oneself to be regarded unfavorably by others
options.html: To appear in a way or make an impression that causes oneself to be regarded unfavorably by others

questions.solution:
The idiom 'In the doldrums' means 'Dull and inactive'. Hence option c) is the correct answer.

'Cut a sorry figure' means 'To appear in a way or make an impression that causes oneself to be regarded unfavorably by others'.

'Paddle one's own canoe' means 'Be independent and self-sufficient'.

'Cutting corners' means 'Doing something poorly in order to save time or money'.

questions.question: Select the correct meaning of the idiom in bold and italics. Trying to interest your son in studying is like beating a dead horse .
questions.questionHtml:

Trying to interest your son in studying is like beating a dead horse.

options.text: Encouraging pupils to increase their study time.
options.html: Encouraging pupils to increase their study time.

options.text: Making futile efforts with no real benefit or consequence.
options.html: Making futile efforts with no real benefit or consequence.

options.text: Doing more than needed or expected.
options.html: Doing more than needed or expected.

questions.solution:
Beating a dead horse: spend time and effort on things that are hopeless and unchangeable.

Among the options, 'making futile efforts with no real benefit or consequence' is the correct option that matches the meaning of the given idiom.

Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Come to the point
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Come to the point

options.text: To speak plainly about the real issue
options.html: To speak plainly about the real issue

options.text: To meet at a designated place
options.html: To meet at a designated place

questions.solution:
The idiom 'come to the point' means 'to reach the main or most important idea of something that is said or written'.

Usage: It took several paragraphs for her to come to the point of her argument.

Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

questions.question: Select the sentence that uses the given idiom correctly. Hit the nail on the head
questions.questionHtml:
Select the sentence that uses the given idiom correctly.

Hit the nail on the head

options.text: He hit the nail on the head when he guessed her age.
options.html: He hit the nail on the head when he guessed her age.

options.text: She hit the nail on the head when she hammered the picture frame.
options.html: She hit the nail on the head when she hammered the picture frame.

options.text: I hit the nail on the head when I couldn't solve the puzzle.
options.html: I hit the nail on the head when I couldn't solve the puzzle.

options.text: They hit the nail on the head when they lost the treasure.
options.html: They hit the nail on the head when they lost the treasure.

questions.solution:
The idiom "hit the nail on the head" means to say or do something exactly right, especially by identifying or describing something accurately. It usually has a positive connotation. Option (a) uses the idiom correctly, as it implies that he made a correct or precise guess. The other options either use the idiom in a literal sense, which is not appropriate or in a way that does not match the meaning of the idiom, which is misleading.

Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.
